prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on where you are in the Phoenix area, how urgent the repair is, the make/model/age of your system, and whether cost, speed, or long warranties matter most. I can, however, help you find the best local contractor for your situation. A few quick questions so I can give a short, tailored list:

- What is your ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix?
- Is this a residential or commercial system?
- What brand/age is the AC (if you know)? What’s happening (no cool air, blowing warm, leaking, tripping breaker, weird noises, etc.)?
- Do you need a same‑day emergency visit, or can it wait for an appointment?
- Do you prefer lowest price, highest-rated service, or brand-authorized dealer?

How to pick the best HVAC company (quick checklist)
- Verify license and insurance: ask for the company’s Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license number and confirm it on the AZ ROC site. Make sure they carry liability and workers’ comp.
- Look for credentials: NATE‑certified technicians, manufacturer-authorized dealer for your AC brand (if applicable).
- Read recent reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi, and check BBB complaints.
- Get at least 3 written estimates that break down parts, labor, and fees.
- Ask about warranties: parts, labor, and any unit replacement guarantees.
- Check response time and 24/7 emergency availability if needed.
- Ask for references from recent customers or examples of similar repairs.

Questions to ask when you call
- What is your ROC license number and proof of insurance?
- Do you charge a diagnosis/service fee? If yes, is that waived if I hire you?
- Are your technicians NATE‑certified?
- Do you give a written estimate and written warranty on parts/labor?
- Are you a dealer or authorized servicer for my equipment brand?
- How soon can you come? Are there after‑hours/emergency fees?

Red flags
- No license or reluctant to provide license/insurance info.
- Extremely low estimate compared to others (bait-and-switch risk).
- Pressure to replace the whole system without diagnosing.
- Cash-only, no receipt, or vague warranty terms.

Typical cost ranges (Phoenix area, ballpark)
- Diagnostic/service call: $75–$200
- Refrigerant recharge: $150–$500 (R‑22 much more if still used)
- Capacitor/contactor replacement: $75–$300
- Condenser or evaporator fan motor: $200–$700
- Compressor replacement: $1,200–$3,000+
- Full AC replacement: $3,500–$12,000+ depending on tonnage and efficiency

Next step
If you want, tell me your ZIP and a brief description of the problem and I’ll give a short list (3–5) of well-reviewed Phoenix HVAC companies you can call and a suggested script to use when getting quotes. I can also help you evaluate any estimates you receive. Which would you prefer?
